Session amc. Exit window: close 2026-11-02 to close 2026-11-03. The AJ Bell 'Nov 3' row is wrong.
conviction_note: Small positive lean. Palantir's own-guide beat pattern (+7.6% vs midpoint in Q2, +8.8% in Q3 2025) against a consensus only 0.8% above the guide, a de-risked tape (-7.4% in the week to Oct 30), no October shutdown and federal-demand proxies outweigh a harsh software reaction function (ServiceNow -15% after hours on Oct 28) and a +50% three-month run-up. The name has sold two of its last four beats, so p_up is held at 53 against a 13-point move; the sum of findings (+0.9) and the scaled number (+0.78) agree in sign and size.
bar: Revenue $2.18bn consensus (TipRanks 2026-10-31 https://www.tipranks.com/news/palantir-q3-earnings-are-on-nov-2-options-traders-brace-for-a-13-3-move-in-pltr-stock ; Koyfin via Stocktwits 2026-11-02 https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/palantir-s-q3-report-to-test-stock-defensiveness-amid-ai-panic-what-analysts-are-expecting/cNG9FfPR92V ; TradingKey 2026-11-02 agree), against the company guide of $2.160-2.164bn revenue and $1.292-1.296bn adjusted operating income (Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001321655/000132165526000039/a2026q2ex991pressrelease.htm). FY2026 guide $8.150-8.158bn implies about $2.42bn for Q4. The EPS bar is disputed: $0.41 (TipRanks, Koyfin) against $0.33 (Nasdaq/Barchart per StockTitan and Heygotrade). Q2 already printed $0.41 adjusted, so $0.33 looks stale. Revenue and the guide are the lines this name trades on, so sizes are not capped for the EPS dispute.
positioning_check: Short interest about 68.1M shares, 2.8% of float (Equibles) or 3.23% (stockanalysis), days to cover 1.9-2.3, mid-August 2026 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/pltr/shortinterest ; https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/PLTR/statistics/). No October settlement was found and Nasdaq's short-interest page returned 503. Not a crowded short. Skew: the baseline was sealed empty (bars_failed) and no 25-delta skew was found; a Benzinga snippet of 2026-11-02 says call volume exceeded puts (page 403, snippet only). Options imply about a 13.3% move (TipRanks 2026-10-31). Run-up: the stock closed $123.06 on 2026-08-01 before Q2 and $184.11 on 2026-10-30 (+50%). The 52-week high of $212.94 was set around Oct 9, and the stock fell 7.4% in the final week before the print (TradingKey 2026-11-02). Stocktwits retail sentiment reads 'bearish'.

findings.finding: Palantir has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide by +7.6% (Q2 2026: $1.935bn vs $1.797-1.801bn) and +8.8% (Q3 2025: $1.181bn vs $1.083-1.087bn), while the Q3 2026 consensus of $2.18bn sits only 0.8% above the $2.162bn guide midpoint. A repeat of that beat puts revenue near $2.30-2.33bn, 5-7% above consensus, against an implied Q4 of about $2.42bn inside the FY guide that would need raising.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Mixed, rebuilt from sources because the baseline history is untrusted. Q2 2026 beat (+7.6% vs guide) and FY raise: about +30% in one day (Stocktwits 2026-11-02). Q3 2025 beat (+8.8% vs guide): shares fell on valuation (TradingView/GuruFocus 2025-11-04). Q1 2026 record quarter: shares declined (Sentisense 2026-05-06). Last four absolute moves averaged 12.79%, range 6.85-29.45% (TipRanks 2026-10-31).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the street knows the beat history ('nine straight beats', 247wallst 2026-10-14), yet the published consensus is still parked about 1% over the guide. If the buy side priced a full repeat, consensus would sit near $2.30bn, or the stock would have held its Oct 9 high into the print instead of falling 14% from it.
findings.independence: Q2 guide from the Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001321655/000132165526000026/a2026q1ex991pressrelease.htm). Analyst revisions over three months ran 22 up and 0 down on revenue (Seeking Alpha via TradingView, https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:da67c4884094b:0-palantir-heads-into-q3-earnings-with-strong-demand-signals-but-valuation-concerns-persist/). Oppenheimer expects a beat and raise (Stocktwits 2026-11-02).

findings.finding: The stock went into the print de-risked after a large run: -6.27% on Oct 30 to $184.11, -7.4% for the week, about 14% below the ~$213 record, after a +50% move from the $123.06 pre-Q2 close (Aug 1). The cause reported was profit-taking plus an almost 5% fall in the tech sector, not company news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 came after a ~40% drawdown from the 2026 high and rose ~30%. Q3 2025 came near a record high and fell. Positioning into the print has tracked the sign of the reaction on the two cases found.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The point is that the bar for a positive reaction is lower than at the Oct 9 high. Had nobody de-risked, the stock would still sit near $209 with a forward P/E above 100x.
findings.independence: Stocktwits 2026-11-02 (bearish retail sentiment; PLTR -1.5% in October vs QQQ -7%) https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/palantir-s-q3-report-to-test-stock-defensiveness-amid-ai-panic-what-analysts-are-expecting/cNG9FfPR92V . Cuts both ways: the +50% three-month run-up is still in the price.

findings.finding: Peer read-through on the reaction function: ServiceNow printed Q3 2026 on Oct 28 with revenue slightly above consensus ($4.11bn vs $4.10bn), adjusted EPS of $1.00 against $1.02 expected, and an AI contract-value forecast raised to $1.7bn, then fell 15.25% after hours. AI-software names are being repriced: per one trader quoted, 9 of the 10 largest AI names sit 10%+ below their three-month highs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: PLTR decoupled from software selloffs in 2026: it rose ~30% in August while software ETFs were weak (Fool 2026-08-05). In the Oct 2026 tech drawdown, however, it fell with the sector.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced through the late-October sector fall. What remains is that the reaction function for a beat that is less than outstanding is harsher than when PLTR jumped 30% in August. A clean read would show PLTR holding up against the -5% tech sector, and it did not.
findings.independence: Stocktwits 2026-11-02 on the 'AI panic' and a trader's 'a beat may not be enough anymore'. Proxy: ServiceNow is seat-based and Palantir is not, so the finding is sized small for that.

findings.finding: Congress passed a continuing resolution on 2026-09-01 that funds the government through 2026-12-11, so there was no Oct 1 shutdown. Last year's Q4 guide was set during the 42-day FY2026 shutdown that began 2025-10-01. The Dec 11 cliff falls inside Palantir's Q4, which could make the Q4 government guide conservative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history on this line. US government revenue grew 90% y/y in Q2 2026 ($809M), and government is ~42% of revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro, and widely known. The company-level transmission is unconfirmed until management speaks to Q4 government. If the street had built in a clean Q4 government quarter, consensus would sit above the implied $2.42bn Q4, and none of the previews quote a Q4 number.
findings.independence: Proxy only. FedTools 'shutdown averted, next cliff Dec 11' https://www.fedtools.com/blog/government-shutdown-october-2026 ; CRS on the FY2026 shutdown https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2026-03-24_R41759_a1672ba6264c7adaec23a2af296bb611f408d7d9.pdf

findings.finding: Federal-demand proxies for the September quarter, the end of the US government fiscal year. An August 2026 Pentagon memo directs up to $244M more for Palantir services through March 2027, and federal obligations to Palantir passed $1bn in FY2026 for the first time (vs $970.5M in 2025). Citi partner checks found a federal partner's tech practice growing above 60% y/y with Palantir among the largest contributors. Oppenheimer models total government growth above 65%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Government strength in Q2 2026 (+90%) came with the +30% reaction. In Q3 2025, government strength did not stop a decline.
findings.why_not_priced: Secondary-source federal data the wires do not aggregate. But the Citi and Oppenheimer views are in notes, so the market has some of it. If priced in full, government growth expectations would be quoted above 65% in previews; they sit at 65%.
findings.independence: Citi partner checks in the Seeking Alpha preview (via TradingView, page undated, Q3 2026 preview) https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:da67c4884094b:0-palantir-heads-into-q3-earnings-with-strong-demand-signals-but-valuation-concerns-persist/ . Oppenheimer in Stocktwits 2026-11-02. The KuCoin item is a CryptoBriefing reprint with no primary document.

findings.finding: RBC (Underperform, $90 target) flags PLTR as the most expensive name in its All-SaaS coverage, at about 61x 2026 and 40x 2027 EV/consensus revenue, and notes investor frustration that there are no meaningful shareholder returns despite about $9bn of cash. The 10-Q shows only $1.5M of repurchases in H1 2026 and $9.2bn of cash and Treasuries.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Valuation concerns were the stated cause of the Q3 2025 post-beat decline (TradingView/GuruFocus 2025-11-04).
findings.why_not_priced: The valuation view is on the wire. The unpriced part is a two-sided option: a buyback announced with the print would be a positive surprise, and its absence keeps the overhang. Signed slightly negative because nothing points to an authorization.

findings.finding: International government headwinds. The UK NHS Federated Data Platform (GBP330m) is under ministerial review with a renewal decision due by December. The London Met GBP50m contract was blocked in May. NYC Health+Hospitals chose not to renew a contract expiring in October 2026. Each could temper the commentary on international and government growth in the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: International has been a small and lagging segment (Q2 implied ~$362M of $1.935bn). It has not driven past reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: UK political news is not in US previews. But it is ~5% of revenue at most, net of a US business growing 90-149%, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Computing.co.uk on the FDP business case https://www.computing.co.uk/news/2026/government/nhs-palantir-platform-s-business-case-under-scrutiny-as-costs-rise-and-benefits-fall ; London Met https://www.localgovernmentlawyer.co.uk/procurement-and-contracts/402-procurement-news/100772-palantir-moves-to-sue-mayor-of-london-over-blocked-met-ai-contract-while-health-secretary-reviews-nhs-deal

findings.finding: Commercial pipeline signals after the Q2 call: Fujitsu became a global FDE partner and AIPCon 11 was held (both Sept 10), Customers Bank is deploying Foundry and AIP (Oct 16), and a Knox Systems FedRAMP partnership was announced (Oct 19, stock +5% that day). None carries a disclosed dollar value.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: US commercial (+149% in Q2) is the line previews call the key metric. Partnership headlines moved the stock +5% on Oct 19, so they are partly priced.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced (the stock rose on Knox). The residual is that the deal count supports the TCV and customer-count line, which previews name as the swing factor.

findings.finding: Balance-sheet visibility in the Q2 10-Q: current deferred revenue $579M at 2026-06-30 vs $409M at 2025-12-31 (+42% in six months), customer deposits $452M vs $357M, RPO $4.9bn with 43% due within 12 months, and TTM customers 1,049 vs 849 a year earlier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observed. Contract-liability growth has accompanied every beat in the series.
findings.why_not_priced: A public document since August, but no preview quotes the deferred-revenue walk. It supports H2 revenue above the guide rather than adding a new fact.
findings.independence: Shares a theme with finding 1 (beat capacity) but not a document. TCV $3.373bn, +49% in the Q2 release.
